Ann and Bob can only do Dev, and Cy can do Ops or QA, so at most two pairs form: Ann–Dev and Cy–Ops, in the accent color with their endpoints. Bob and QA stay unmatched. The card lists the two pairs and the size 2." width="100%"} In a bipartite graph the nodes split into two sides and every edge joins the two sides, as in workers and jobs, students and schools, or reviewers and papers. A maximum matching pairs as many nodes across the sides as possible, with each node in at most one pair. This method finds one with the Hopcroft-Karp algorithm, which is much faster than the general `maximum_weight_matching()` on large bipartite graphs. The sides are found by 2-coloring the graph (ignoring edge direction) unless they are given with `top_nodes=`. The size of a maximum matching does not depend on which valid split is used. Self-loops are not allowed (they make a graph non-bipartite). ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [top_nodes]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional list of the nodes on one side (IDs or labels); all other nodes form the other side. If `None` (default), the sides are found automatically. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The IDs of the matched edges, in ascending order. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is not bipartite, or `top_nodes=` leaves an edge within one side. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Hopcroft and Karp (1973) augment along many shortest augmenting paths at once: each phase runs a breadth-first search from all free top nodes to layer the graph, then a depth-first search finds a maximal set of vertex-disjoint shortest augmenting paths in that layering. Only $O(\sqrt{V})$ phases are needed, so the running time is $O(E \sqrt{V})$. By König's theorem the matching size equals the size of a minimum vertex cover (see `bipartite_vertex_cover()`). ## Examples {.doc-examples} Three applicants and three jobs. Ann and Bob can only do the first job between them, so at most two of the three jobs can be filled: ::: {#66bad2b7 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph().add_nodes(["Ann", "Bob", "Cy", "Dev", "Ops", "QA"]) g.add_edges([("Ann", "Dev"), ("Bob", "Dev"), ("Cy", "Ops"), ("Cy", "QA")]) matching = g.bipartite_maximum_matching(top_nodes=["Ann", "Bob", "Cy"]) len(matching) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 2 ``` ::: ::: Listing the pairs shows that Cy takes one of their two jobs: ::: {#1c433036 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} [tuple(g.get_label_from_id(n) for n in g.get_node_ids_by_edge_id(e)) for e in matching] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` [('Ann', 'Dev'), ('Cy', 'Ops')] ``` ::: :::
